[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/21 (Sun) 12:29  
[USER] User is looking for inspiration for a pasta salad recipe.  
[PREFERENCE] User has a preference for goat cheese, which they used in their last pasta salad and was a huge hit.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Goat cheese is an excellent choice to pair with sun-dried tomatoes, as its tangy creaminess complements the chewy, savory flavor of the tomatoes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested marinades for grilled chicken that would pair well with sun-dried tomatoes and goat cheese:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Herby Italian-Style Marinade: olive oil, minced garlic, chopped fresh rosemary, thyme, oregano, salt, and pepper.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Lemon-Herb Marinade: lemon juice, olive oil, minced garlic, chopped fresh parsley, salt, and pepper.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Balsamic Glaze Marinade: balsamic glaze, olive oil, minced garlic, and salt.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Mediterranean-Style Marinade: olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, chopped Kalamata olives, artichoke hearts, and oregano.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Spicy Italian-Style Marinade: olive oil, minced garlic, diced jalapeño, chopped fresh basil, salt, and pepper.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] These marinades will give the grilled chicken a delicious flavor that pairs beautifully with the sun-dried tomatoes and goat cheese.  
[PREFERENCE] User is interested in trying out the Herby Italian-Style Marinade.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended Italian-style pasta shapes that would hold up well to the grilled chicken, sun-dried tomatoes, and goat cheese:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Penne: tube shape and ridged texture.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Fusilli: corkscrew shape.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Farfalle: bow-tie shape.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Rotini: spiral shape.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Cavatappi: rustic, homemade texture.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested adding toasted pine nuts or chopped fresh parsley for crunch and freshness, along with a drizzle of good olive oil and a sprinkle of salt.  
[PREFERENCE] User has previously had penne in other pasta salads and found it works well.
